# `entire dispatch` — Design

**Date:** 2026-04-16
**Status:** Draft — awaiting review

## Summary

A new top-level CLI command, `entire dispatch`, that summarizes recent agent work into a dispatch-shaped bullet list. Default output is deterministic and paste-ready. An opt-in `--generate` flag calls an LLM to produce a full voice-styled dispatch (themed sections, opener, closer). Works on the current repo by default, scales out to explicit local paths via `--repos` and to entire GitHub orgs via `--org`.

Primary use case: users who publish a recurring dispatch/newsletter/update (like the [Entire Dispatch](https://entire.io/blog/entire-dispatch-0x0009)) get the bullet material generated from their actual shipped work without manually trawling `git log`, checkpoints, or PRs.

## Motivation

Existing surfaces don't cover this:

- `entire explain` — per-checkpoint deep-dive.
- `entire search` — cloud-backed, query-driven, per-result.
- `entire sessions` — live session management.
- `entire trail` — branch-level work tracking.

None of them produce a **multi-checkpoint rollup** shaped like a dispatch. The server-side checkpoint analysis pipeline (see analysis-endpoints PR) already generates per-checkpoint labels and 2–4 sentence summaries; `entire dispatch` consumes those to produce the rollup locally.

## Non-goals

- Replacing the server-side analysis pipeline — this command consumes it, not duplicates it.
- Publishing the dispatch anywhere (no Discord/Slack/email integration). Output is text to stdout; the user pastes it wherever.
- Editing or approving individual bullets. The user is expected to tweak the output manually if they want to ship it as-is.
- Supporting fully offline/no-login use. Login is hard-required.

## Command surface

```
entire dispatch [flags]
```

### Scope flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--since <duration-or-date>` | `7d` | Time window. Accepts Go duration (`7d`, `168h`, `2w`) and git-style strings (`"2 days ago"`, `"1 week"`, `2026-04-09`). Filters on checkpoint `created_at`. |
| `--all-branches` | off | Include checkpoints from all branches. Default: only branches containing current HEAD. |
| `--repos <path1,path2,…>` | current repo | Comma-separated list of local repo paths. Each must be Entire-enabled; non-enabled paths are warned and skipped. Mutually exclusive with `--org`. |
| `--org <name>` | — | Cloud-driven: enumerate every checkpoint you have access to whose repo belongs to this org. Requires login. Mutually exclusive with `--repos`. |

### Output flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--generate` | off | Synthesize bullets into a voice-styled dispatch via LLM (opener + themed sections + bullets + closer). |
| `--voice <file>` | neutral | Markdown file with freeform tone instructions for `--generate`. Without `--voice`, uses a neutral "product update" voice. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Show what checkpoints and labels would be fed to generation. Works with or without `--generate`. Makes no LLM calls and no cloud analysis fetches. |
| `--json` | off | Emit structured data (checkpoints, analyses, labels, files) instead of text. |

### Behavior flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--wait` | off | Block until pending/generating analyses complete (5-min cap). Default: skip + warn. |

### Auth

Hard require. Without a token, errors with `"run \`entire login\`"`. Same pattern as `entire search`.

### Examples

```
entire dispatch
entire dispatch --since "last monday"
entire dispatch --all-branches --since 14d
entire dispatch --repos ~/Projects/cli,~/Projects/web
entire dispatch --org entireio --since 1w
entire dispatch --generate --voice ~/dotfiles/dispatch-voice.md
entire dispatch --dry-run --since 2w
entire dispatch --json > dispatch.json
```

## Data flow

### Bullet source (fallback chain)

For each checkpoint in the time window, resolve bullet text and section label via this chain:

1. **Cloud analysis** — `POST /api/v1/users/me/checkpoints/analyses/batch` with `{repoFullName, checkpointIds}`.
   - `status: complete` → use first `summary` block as bullet text, `labels` for section grouping.
   - `status: pending` or `generating` → skip with per-checkpoint warning; counted and reported at end of output. With `--wait`, poll until complete (5-min cap).
   - `status: failed` → fall through to step 2.
   - `404` (unknown to backend, i.e., unpushed) → fall through to step 2. Count as "unpushed" for the end-of-output nudge.
2. **Local summarize title** — if summarization is enabled (`settings.IsSummarizeEnabled()`) and a `Summary.Title` exists for the checkpoint in `entire/checkpoints/v1/<id>/…/metadata.json`, use it. No labels → checkpoint lands in a flat "Updates" section for its repo.
3. **Commit message subject** — if the checkpoint has an associated commit via the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, use the subject line. No labels → "Updates".
4. **None of the above** — omit the checkpoint from output. Count reported at end: `"N uncategorized checkpoints skipped."`

### Cloud calls

- **Batch analyses**: one call per repo, up to 200 IDs. Paginate over 200.
- **Org enumeration** (for `--org`): a new endpoint, `GET /api/v1/orgs/:org/checkpoints?since=<iso>&limit=…&cursor=…`, which returns `{checkpoints: [{id, repo_full_name, created_at}], cursor}`. **This endpoint may not exist yet**; landing it is a prerequisite to shipping `--org`. The rest of the command can ship without it.

### Unpushed-checkpoint detection

After batch fetch, any checkpoint that returns 404/unknown from the cloud is considered unpushed. If the count is > 0 and output is text (not `--json`), a single-line nudge is appended:

```
⚠ 7 checkpoints weren't pushed — run `git push origin entire/checkpoints/v1` for richer analysis next run.
```

## Output format

### Default output (no `--generate`)

Plain, dispatch-shaped. Sections are `<repo-name>/` at the top level, then label-based subsections if cloud analyses supplied labels; otherwise a flat "Updates" block per repo.

```
entire dispatch  (7 days, current repo, current branch)

cli/
  CI & Tooling
    • CI tests no longer hang on TTY detection during local runs.
    • Nightly workflow now fails instead of silently skipping when tag exists.
    • Added Vercel preview deploy config for the frontend.

  Hooks & Messaging
    • Hook system messages reworded from "Powered by Entire" to "Entire CLI".

  Settings
    • Summary provider is persisted to local settings and respected by `entire configure`.

13 checkpoints · 4 branches · 23 files touched
⚠ 2 checkpoints weren't pushed — run `git push origin entire/checkpoints/v1` for richer analysis next run.
```

### `--generate` output

LLM pass stitches the same bullet data into a voice-styled dispatch. One call to the existing `summarize.ClaudeGenerator` with a dispatch-specific system prompt. Without `--voice`, neutral "product update" voice. With `--voice <file>`, the file's content is injected into the system prompt as voice guidance.

```
Beep, boop. Marvin here. Another week of entropy successfully postponed — this time across the CLI, mostly.

## CI & Tooling
- CI tests no longer hang on TTY detection during local runs.
- Nightly release workflow now fails instead of silently skipping.
- Added Vercel preview deploy config for the frontend.

## Hooks & Messaging
- Hook system messages reworded from "Powered by Entire" to "Entire CLI".

## Settings
- Summary provider is persisted to local settings and respected by `entire configure`.

— Until next week. The heat death of the universe remains roughly on schedule.
```

### `--json` output

Structured payload with all source data, suitable for piping and scripting:

```json
{
  "generated_at": "2026-04-16T14:32:00Z",
  "window": {"since": "2026-04-09T00:00:00Z", "until": "2026-04-16T14:32:00Z"},
  "repos": [
    {
      "full_name": "entireio/cli",
      "path": "/Users/.../cli",
      "sections": [
        {
          "label": "CI & Tooling",
          "bullets": [
            {
              "checkpoint_id": "a3b2c4d5e6f7",
              "text": "CI tests no longer hang on TTY detection during local runs.",
              "source": "cloud_analysis",
              "branch": "main",
              "commit_sha": "700aace0f",
              "files_touched": ["cmd/entire/cli/summarize/summarize.go"],
              "created_at": "2026-04-14T18:23:00Z",
              "labels": ["CI & Tooling"]
            }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "skipped": {"pending": 0, "unpushed": 2, "uncategorized": 0}
    }
  ],
  "totals": {"checkpoints": 13, "branches": 4, "files_touched": 23}
}
```

### `--dry-run` output

Compact listing of what *would* be fetched/generated. No cloud calls, no LLM calls:

```
entire dispatch --dry-run  (7 days, current repo, current branch)

Would fetch analyses for 13 checkpoints across 1 repo:

cli/
  a3b2c4d5e6f7  main         2026-04-14  Fix hanging CI tests locally
  b4c5d6e7f8a9  soph/fix     2026-04-14  fix hanging summary tty in local tests
  …

Would NOT call the LLM (no --generate).
```

render.go         # text + --json renderers

- **Default**: server-side generation (entire.io uses its own tokens/money). CLI calls a new API endpoint, gets back structured data, renders it.
- **`--local`**: generate locally using the user's own LLM tokens. All the data-flow we designed (per-checkpoint analyses → fallback chain → local render) still applies, it's just gated behind this flag now.
- Server-generated dispatches also render on entire.io — CLI can print a web URL.

Let me update the spec for this split.

input.old_string:
## Summary

A new top-level CLI command, `entire dispatch`, that summarizes recent agent work into a dispatch-shaped bullet list. Default output is deterministic and paste-ready. An opt-in `--generate` flag calls an LLM to produce a full voice-styled dispatch (themed sections, opener, closer). Works on the current repo by default, scales out to explicit local paths via `--repos` and to entire GitHub orgs via `--org`.

Primary use case: users who publish a recurring dispatch/newsletter/update (like the [Entire Dispatch](https://entire.io/blog/entire-dispatch-0x0009)) get the bullet material generated from their actual shipped work without manually trawling `git log`, checkpoints, or PRs.
input.new_string:
## Summary

A new top-level CLI command, `entire dispatch`, that summarizes recent agent work into a dispatch-shaped bullet list.

**Default path — server-side generation.** The CLI calls a new entire.io endpoint, which enumerates checkpoints, consumes the existing per-checkpoint analyses, and (with `--generate`) synthesizes voice-styled prose using Entire's tokens. The same dispatch is also viewable on entire.io's web UI. CLI prints a URL to the web view alongside the rendered output.

**`--local` flag — local generation.** Bypasses the server entirely. CLI enumerates checkpoints from the local `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch, batch-fetches per-checkpoint analyses (read-only), assembles bullets via a fallback chain, and (with `--generate`) calls the user's own LLM. User pays the tokens.

Works on the current repo by default, scales out to explicit local paths via `--repos` (requires `--local`), and to entire GitHub orgs via `--org`.

Primary use case: users who publish a recurring dispatch/newsletter/update (like the [Entire Dispatch](https://entire.io/blog/entire-dispatch-0x0009)) get the bullet material generated from their actual shipped work without manually trawling `git log`, checkpoints, or PRs.

### Output flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--generate` | off | Synthesize bullets into a voice-styled dispatch via LLM (opener + themed sections + bullets + closer). |
| `--voice <value>` | neutral | Voice/tone guidance for `--generate`. Accepts either a path to a markdown file OR a literal inline description. Detection: if the value resolves to a readable file on disk, its content is used; otherwise the value is treated as a literal string. Without `--voice`, uses a neutral "product update" voice. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Show what checkpoints and labels would be fed to generation. Works with or without `--generate`. Makes no LLM calls and no cloud analysis fetches. |
| `--format <text\|markdown\|json>` | `text` | Output format. `text` = plain-text with `•` bullets and indented sections, suitable for terminals. `markdown` = pure markdown (`#` headers, `-` bullets, fenced where appropriate), paste-friendly for docs and blog posts. `json` = structured payload (checkpoints, analyses, labels, files) for pipelines. |
input.new_string:
### Output flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--generate` | off | Synthesize bullets into a voice-styled dispatch via LLM (opener + themed sections + bullets + closer). In default mode, the server runs the LLM (Entire's tokens). In `--local` mode, the CLI runs the user's configured LLM (user's tokens). |
| `--voice <value>` | neutral | Voice/tone guidance for `--generate`. Accepts either a path to a markdown file OR a literal inline description. Detection: if the value resolves to a readable file on disk, its content is used; otherwise the value is treated as a literal string. Without `--voice`, uses a neutral "product update" voice. In default mode, passed to the server in the request body; in `--local` mode, used directly. |
| `--dry-run` | off | Show what checkpoints and labels would be fed to generation. Works with or without `--generate`. Makes no LLM calls and no cloud analysis fetches. In default mode, issues a dry-run request to the server (server returns scope preview without calling its LLM). |
| `--format <text\|markdown\|json>` | `text` | Output format. `text` = plain-text with `•` bullets and indented sections, suitable for terminals. `markdown` = pure markdown (`#` headers, `-` bullets, fenced where appropriate), paste-friendly for docs and blog posts. `json` = structured payload (checkpoints, analyses, labels, files) for pipelines. Rendering happens client-side in both modes — the server always returns the structured payload, and the CLI's renderer produces the requested format. |

## Data flow

Two paths: server-side (default) and local (`--local`). Both produce the same structured payload shape, which the CLI renders consistently.

### Server-side path (default)

1. CLI resolves the scope locally: determines the current repo's `owner/name` from `git remote` (or uses `--org`), collects `--since`, `--branches`, `--voice`, etc.
2. CLI issues a single call: `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` with body `{repo: "<owner/name>"|null, org: "<name>"|null, since: <ISO>, branches: [...]|"all", generate: bool, voice: "<string>"|null, dry_run: bool}`.
3. Server enumerates checkpoints, consumes analyses (already cached per-checkpoint), optionally runs its LLM for `--generate`, persists the result (so entire.io can show it), and returns the structured payload plus a `web_url` pointing at the web view.
4. CLI renders to `--format`, prints the web URL at the end in `text`/`markdown` modes.

Server path requirements:
- New endpoint `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` — see Server-side prerequisites below.
- Server stores dispatches for web display (persistence detail is owned by the server spec, not this one).

+4. CLI renders to `--format`, prints the web URL at the end in `text`/`markdown` modes.

## Edge cases & error handling
| Case | Behavior |

input.old_string:
| Case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| No checkpoints in window | Print `"No checkpoints in the last Nd."` · exit 0 |
| `--repos` path isn't a git repo | Per-path error with path name, continue with remaining paths |
| `--repos` path is a git repo but not Entire-enabled | Warn + skip, continue |
| `--org` with no indexed checkpoints | Empty output with "try widening `--since`" hint · exit 0 |
| Network error during cloud fetch | Abort with clear error (don't silently fall back — user should know) |
| `--wait` timeout (5 min) | Progress ticks while waiting; error out if still incomplete |
| `--generate` with zero eligible checkpoints | Skip LLM call, print same "no checkpoints" message |
| Auth token missing | Error: `"dispatch requires login — run \`entire login\`"` |
| Auth token expired/revoked | Error: `"login expired — run \`entire login\`"` |
| `--repos` and `--org` both passed | Error: `"--repos and --org are mutually exclusive"` |
| `--format json` and `--generate` both passed | Allowed — JSON payload includes a `generated_text` field with the LLM output |
| `--format json` and `--dry-run` both passed | Allowed — JSON version of dry-run payload (no cloud/LLM calls) |
| `--voice` without `--generate` | Error: `"--voice requires --generate"` |
| `--voice <value>` as a file path that looks like a file but can't be read | Error before any cloud calls. If the value has no path separators and doesn't resolve to a file, it's treated as a literal string (no error). |
| `--branches <list>` where a listed branch doesn't exist | Warn per missing branch, continue with remaining branches |
| `--format <value>` not in `text\|markdown\|json` | Error with list of valid values |

## Interactive wizard

`entire dispatch` with no flags on a TTY auto-enters a `huh`-based wizard. Matches the codebase convention (`entire sessions stop`, `entire search`). With any flag passed, or stdin piped, the wizard is skipped and the command runs non-interactively.

### Trigger rules

- **Wizard ON** — stdin is a TTY AND no flags have been explicitly set.
- **Wizard OFF** — any flag passed (including flags with default-equal values), stdin is piped, or `ACCESSIBLE=1` with no flags (accessible mode uses `NewAccessibleForm()` internally, so wizard still shows but in accessible form).

### Step sequence

1. **Source mode** — Server (default, Entire's tokens) / Local (user's tokens). Maps to `--local`.
2. **Scope** — Current repo / Specific repos (disabled in server mode) / Whole org (prompts for org name) / Custom (jump to freeform flag review).
3. **Time window** — Last 24h / Last 7d (default) / Last 30d / Custom (text input accepting git-style or ISO).
4. **Branches** — Current branch / All branches / Select specific (multi-select from local refs).
5. **Generate prose?** — Bullets only / Generate full dispatch with voice (default in wizard). Maps to `--generate`. If "bullets only", skip step 6.
6. **Voice** (only shown if step 5 = generate) — Neutral product update (default) / Marvin (sardonic AI, Entire Dispatch style) / Custom (text input) / Load from markdown file (file picker).
7. **Format** — Text (default) / Markdown / JSON.
8. **Confirm & run** — Shows the equivalent CLI command, then asks: Run it now (default) / Copy command to clipboard and exit / Edit flags (jumps back to step 1) / Cancel.

Every step has a default that works on Enter; power users can tab through in a few seconds.

### Built-in voice presets

Shipped with the CLI binary via `go:embed`:

```
cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/voices/
  neutral.md       # neutral product-update tone (default)
  marvin.md        # sardonic AI companion, inspired by the Entire Dispatch
```

`--voice` value resolution (unchanged from command surface, repeated here for completeness): preset name (case-insensitive) → file path → literal string.

Adding more presets later: drop a new `.md` into `voices/`, register in a small map. No API changes.

### Accessibility

- All `huh` forms wrapped with the existing `NewAccessibleForm()` helper so `ACCESSIBLE=1` works without extra code per step.
- Escape at any step cancels the wizard cleanly (exit 130, no partial state written).

### Always-print equivalent command

The confirm screen always shows the full CLI command that the wizard assembled. Rationale:

- Users learn the flag syntax organically.
- "Copy command" option lets users drop the command into aliases / CI / scripts without going through the wizard each time.
- Useful for debugging and support ("run `entire dispatch --since 7d --branches main…` and paste the output").

### Wizard-specific tests

- **Step golden files** (`wizard_test.go`) — each step's prompt rendered as a fixture (TUI snapshot).
- **Full flow integration** — scripted stdin drives the wizard through a happy path and asserts the equivalent CLI command output matches expectations.
- **Flag-skip behavior** — any flag passed short-circuits the wizard; verified for each flag.
- **Accessible mode** — `ACCESSIBLE=1` renders plain text prompts, tested with golden output.
- **Cancel paths** — escape at each step cleans up and exits 130.

## Implementation plan

To be produced via the `writing-plans` skill once this spec is approved.

- **B. Repo-scoped** — anyone with access to the repo(s) covered by the dispatch. Matches how checkpoints/trails work on entire.io today.
- **C. Org-scoped** — anyone in the org. Makes cross-repo dispatches natural.
- **D. Unlisted shareable URL** — creator decides; URL acts as the capability. Login not required to view (but required to create).
- **E. Public** — SEO-indexable. Probably only useful for published product-update dispatches like the real Entire Dispatch blog.

Most products combine 2–3. A likely starting set: **B + D** (default is repo/org-scoped, creator can flip a dispatch to unlisted for sharing externally).

- **F. CLI-only** — only `entire dispatch` creates a record. Web UI just reads.
- **G. Web-also** — a "New dispatch" button on entire.io opens a web form that runs the same server endpoint. Duplicates the wizard, but discoverable for users who haven't installed the CLI.
- **H. Web + edit existing** — web can create, and also edit the LLM-generated prose before "publishing" (changing status from draft to visible).

# `dispatch` web UI on entire.io — Design

**Date:** 2026-04-16
**Status:** Draft — awaiting review
**Companion spec:** [`2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md`](./2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md) (the CLI + backend endpoint)

## Summary

Web UI on entire.io for viewing, browsing, and creating dispatches. Three core pages:

1. **Detail page** (`/dispatches/:id`) — URL-shareable rendered dispatch with metadata sidebar.
2. **Personal feed** (`/dispatches`) — chronological list of dispatches the viewer has access to, with filters.
3. **Create form** (`/dispatches/new`) — web equivalent of the CLI wizard. Calls the same `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` endpoint the CLI uses.

Plus a per-repo index (`/gh/:org/:repo/dispatches`) reusing the same card layout pre-filtered to the repo, consistent with how `checkpoints`, `trails`, and `runners` already live under `_repo/gh/`.

**Repo / codebase** — the entire.io frontend (`/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/analysis-chunk-merge`), not the CLI repo. Per the project convention, all backend routes and frontend pages for this feature must be developed from a worktree off that path.

## Goals

- Let users view a generated dispatch via a URL (share with teammates, link from CLI `web_url` response).
- Let users browse dispatches they have access to, filtered by repo / date / creator.
- Let users who haven't installed the CLI create a dispatch from the web (same fields as the wizard).
- Blend into the existing entire.io navigation alongside checkpoints, trails, runners.

## Non-goals

- Editing dispatch prose. v1 is read-only; to get different prose, regenerate with different flags.
- Commenting / reactions / social features. Out of scope.
- Public (non-authenticated) dispatch pages. Everything requires login.
- Real-time collaborative editing. N/A (no editing).

## Access control

**Strict** — a user can view a dispatch only if they have access to **every** repo the dispatch covers. For an `--org`-scoped dispatch, this means access to every repo in the org at the time of rendering.

Server enforces access on:

- `GET /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` (list) — returns only dispatches the viewer passes the strict check for.
- `GET /api/v1/dispatches/:id` (detail) — 404 on access failure (not 403 — don't leak existence).
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` (create) — creator must have access to all covered repos at creation time. The created dispatch snapshots the access boundary; if the creator later loses access to one of the repos, they still see it (history preservation).

## Routes

| Route | Purpose | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| `/dispatches` | Personal feed — all dispatches viewer has access to | `_authenticated` |
| `/dispatches/new` | Create form | `_authenticated` |
| `/dispatches/:id` | Detail page | `_authenticated` + strict access check |
| `/gh/:org/:repo/dispatches` | Per-repo filtered index | `_authenticated` + repo access check |

Follows the existing TanStack Router conventions in the codebase (`_authenticated/*.tsx`, `_repo/gh/$org.$repo.*.tsx`).

## Pages

### Detail page — `/dispatches/:id`

**Layout**: two-column. Main column renders the dispatch markdown (same payload as `--format markdown` from the CLI). Right sidebar (280px) shows metadata.

**Main column** — rendered markdown:

- Title: `Weekly dispatch — entireio/cli` (or similar; generated or user-provided)
- Meta line under title: date range · branches · checkpoint count · file count
- Body: themed sections with bullets (same as CLI output)
- When generated with a voice preset, voice intro/outro render with a subtle visual treatment (e.g., italic + colored bar) so voice-authored lines are distinguishable from bullet content.

**Sidebar** sections, top to bottom:

- **Creator** — avatar, name, `@handle`, "2h ago" relative time.
- **Scope** — repo badges, window, branches, voice name.
- **Actions** (buttons):
  - `Regenerate` (primary) — reruns the same scope + voice; new dispatch, keeps original. Loading state inline.
  - `Copy markdown` — clipboard copy of the raw markdown payload.
  - `Open in CLI` — opens a modal showing the equivalent `entire dispatch …` command with a Copy button.
  - `Copy share link` — copies the current URL.

**Empty / error states**:

- Dispatch not found or no access → 404 page (same layout as rest of site).
- Dispatch still generating → loading skeleton, poll status every 2s, render when complete.
- Generation failed → error card with reason + "Retry" button.

### Personal feed — `/dispatches`

**Layout**: one-column list.

**Header** — "Dispatches" + filter bar:

- Repo filter (multi-select, default "All repos")
- Date range (preset: Last 7d / Last 30d / All time, or custom)
- Creator filter (default "Anyone"; "Me" / specific user)
- Search input (matches title and body text, via existing search infrastructure if available)
- `+ New dispatch` button (right-aligned, primary) → `/dispatches/new`

**Cards** — one per dispatch:

- Avatar (creator's, colored gradient if no photo)
- Title (first heading of the dispatch or autogenerated from scope)
- Body preview (~180 chars of the rendered text)
- Footer row: repo badges, checkpoint count, voice name
- Date column on the right (relative time + window)
- Click → `/dispatches/:id`

**Empty state**: "No dispatches yet. Generate your first with `entire dispatch` in the CLI, or [create one here](/dispatches/new)."

**Pagination**: infinite scroll or `Load more` button. 20 per page.

### Per-repo index — `/gh/:org/:repo/dispatches`

Same card layout as Personal feed, pre-filtered to the repo. Accessible from the repo sidebar alongside Checkpoints / Trails / Runners.

### Create form — `/dispatches/new`

**Layout**: two-column. Main column is the form, right column (340px) is the live preview.

**Form** (grouped into fieldsets):

- **Scope**
  - Repos / Org toggle (pill selector). Default: repos, pre-filled with the current repo if the user is navigating from `/gh/:org/:repo/dispatches`.
  - Time window — pill row: 24h / 7d (default) / 30d / Custom (opens date picker).
  - Branches — pill row: Default (current) / All / Select… (opens multi-select).
- **Output**
  - Format — pill row: Markdown (default) / Text / JSON.
  - Generate prose? — Bullets only / Generate with voice (default).
  - Voice — card grid: Neutral · Marvin · Custom description · Upload .md. One card selected at a time.

**Preview panel** (right column):

- Live "what this will cover" stats: repos, branches, window, checkpoints count, files touched, unpushed count (if any).
- Equivalent CLI command rendered in a monospace block — updates as fields change. Copy button.

**Buttons**:

- `Generate dispatch` (primary) — submits; shows inline loading, redirects to detail page on completion.
- `Preview (dry-run)` (secondary) — calls the dispatch endpoint with `dry_run: true`, renders the would-be output inline (not persisted, no LLM call).

**Validation**:

- Repo/org field required.
- Custom window requires valid date parsing.
- Voice "Upload .md" requires a file < 50KB of markdown.
- Errors show inline with the relevant field, not a global banner.

## Component architecture

Follows the existing domain-per-feature pattern in `frontend/src/domains/platform/`:

```
frontend/src/domains/platform/dispatches/
  index.ts                            # public exports
  api.ts                              # client for /api/v1/…/dispatches
  api.test.ts
  routeConfig.ts                      # TanStack route config
  breadcrumbs.ts
  breadcrumbs.test.ts
  components/
    DispatchDetail.tsx                # rendered markdown + sidebar container
    DispatchSidebar.tsx               # creator / scope / actions
    DispatchCard.tsx                  # feed card
    DispatchFilterBar.tsx             # filters on feed page
    DispatchForm.tsx                  # create form
    DispatchPreviewPane.tsx           # live preview on create page
    VoicePicker.tsx                   # voice card selector
    RegenerateButton.tsx              # async action button with status
    OpenInCliModal.tsx                # "open in cli" modal w/ copy command
  hooks/
    useDispatch.ts                    # fetch single dispatch + polling if generating
    useDispatchList.ts                # list w/ filters
    useCreateDispatch.ts              # mutation
    useDispatchPreview.ts             # dry-run mutation
  pages/
    DispatchDetailPage.tsx
    DispatchDetailPage.test.tsx

**Status:** Draft — awaiting review
**Companion spec:** [`2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md`](./2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md) (the CLI + backend endpoint)

## Summary

Web UI on entire.io for viewing, browsing, and creating dispatches. Three core pages:

1. **Detail page** (`/dispatches/:id`) — URL-shareable rendered dispatch with metadata sidebar.
2. **Personal feed** (`/dispatches`) — chronological list of dispatches the viewer has access to, with filters.
3. **Create form** (`/dispatches/new`) — web equivalent of the CLI wizard. Calls the same `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` endpoint the CLI uses.

Plus a per-repo index (`/gh/:org/:repo/dispatches`) reusing the same card layout pre-filtered to the repo, consistent with how `checkpoints`, `trails`, and `runners` already live under `_repo/gh/`.

**Repo / codebase** — the entire.io frontend (`/Users/alisha/Projects/wt/entire.io/analysis-chunk-merge`), not the CLI repo. Per the project convention, all backend routes and frontend pages for this feature must be developed from a worktree off that path.

## Goals

- Let users view a generated dispatch via a URL (share with teammates, link from CLI `web_url` response).
- Let users browse dispatches they have access to, filtered by repo / date / creator.
- Let users who haven't installed the CLI create a dispatch from the web (same fields as the wizard).
- Blend into the existing entire.io navigation alongside checkpoints, trails, runners.

## Non-goals

- Editing dispatch prose. v1 is read-only; to get different prose, regenerate with different flags.
- Commenting / reactions / social features. Out of scope.
- Public (non-authenticated) dispatch pages. Everything requires login.
- Real-time collaborative editing. N/A (no editing).

## Access control

**Strict** — a user can view a dispatch only if they have access to **every** repo the dispatch covers. For an `--org`-scoped dispatch, this means access to every repo in the org at the time of rendering.

Server enforces access on:

- `GET /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` (list) — returns only dispatches the viewer passes the strict check for.
- `GET /api/v1/dispatches/:id` (detail) — 404 on access failure (not 403 — don't leak existence).
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` (create) — creator must have access to all covered repos at creation time. The created dispatch snapshots the access boundary; if the creator later loses access to one of the repos, they still see it (history preservation).

| Route | Purpose | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| `/dispatches` | Personal feed — all dispatches viewer has access to | `_authenticated` |
| `/dispatches/new` | Create form | `_authenticated` |

### Detail page — `/dispatches/:id`

**Layout**: two-column. Main column renders the dispatch markdown (same payload as `--format markdown` from the CLI). Right sidebar (280px) shows metadata.

**Main column** — rendered markdown:

- Title: `Weekly dispatch — entireio/cli` (or similar; generated or user-provided)
- Meta line under title: date range · branches · checkpoint count · file count
- Body: themed sections with bullets (same as CLI output)

- **Creator** — avatar, name, `@handle`, "2h ago" relative time.
- **Scope** — repo badges, window, branches, voice name.
- **Actions** (buttons):

  - `Copy markdown` — clipboard copy of the raw markdown payload.
  - `Open in CLI` — opens a modal showing the equivalent `entire dispatch …` command with a Copy button.
  - `Copy share link` — copies the current URL.

- Equivalent CLI command rendered in a monospace block — updates as fields change. Copy button.

- `Generate dispatch` (primary) — submits; shows inline loading, redirects to detail page on completion.
- `Preview (dry-run)` (secondary) — calls the dispatch endpoint with `dry_run: true`, renders the would-be output inline (not persisted, no LLM call).

# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

No-ship: the specs still leave cross-repo authorization, write idempotency, and failure classification loose enough to leak data, create duplicate dispatch records, or hide permission problems as "unpushed" local state.

Findings:
- [high] Cross-repo enumeration/create flows are specified with authentication but not authorization (specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md:169-172)
  The CLI spec introduces org-wide enumeration and server-side dispatch creation for arbitrary `repo`/`org` scopes, but the contract only hard-requires a login token and never says the backend must prove the caller can see every repo included in that scope. If implemented literally, an authenticated user could request dispatches for repos/orgs outside their tenancy, or the server could silently include repos it should have filtered out. This is a tenant-isolation gap, not just a UX omission.
  Recommendation: Make repo-level authorization explicit for every new server endpoint: `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` and `GET /api/v1/orgs/:org/checkpoints` must filter or reject any repo the caller cannot access, and the spec should require tests for mixed-access org scopes.
- [high] Default dispatch generation persists new records without any idempotency or cleanup model (specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md:147-150)
  The default CLI path is a mutating `POST` that persists a dispatch record every time the command runs, and the product model also creates fresh records on regenerate. The spec later adds automatic retry on server 5xx, but never adds idempotency keys, dedupe semantics, or any delete/archive path. A transient retry, double-submit, or repeated CLI run against the same scope will produce multiple indistinguishable dispatchs and share URLs, polluting the feed with irreversible duplicates.
  Recommendation: Split preview/render from persistent creation, or require an idempotency key derived from scope+window+voice+generate inputs with server-side dedupe. Also specify whether users can delete/archive duplicate dispatches.
- [medium] `404` is overloaded as "unpushed" in the CLI flow, which will mask authorization failures as local-state issues (specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md:160-167)
  The local-mode fallback treats a `404` from the batch-analysis API as proof that a checkpoint is merely unpushed and tells the user to `git push`. But the companion web spec already uses `404` to hide unauthorized resources instead of leaking existence. If the batch/org APIs follow the same access-control pattern, pushed checkpoints from repos the caller no longer has access to will be silently dropped and misreported as "unpushed," making real permission failures hard to detect and recover from. This finding depends on the reasonable inference that the new APIs will follow the same anti-enumeration convention.
  Recommendation: Define a distinct per-checkpoint status for `forbidden`/`not_visible` separate from `unknown`/`unpushed`, and require the CLI to surface permission failures separately instead of folding them into the push hint.

Next steps:
- Specify mandatory repo-level authorization rules for all new dispatch/org endpoints.
- Add idempotent create semantics or a non-persistent preview/read path before shipping.
- Separate unauthorized vs unpushed checkpoint states in the batch-analysis contract.

  The default CLI path is a mutating `POST` that persists a dispatch record every time the command runs, and the product model also creates fresh records on regenerate. The spec later adds automatic retry on server 5xx, but never adds idempotency keys, dedupe semantics, or any delete/archive path. A transient retry, double-submit, or repeated CLI run against the same scope will produce multiple indistinguishable dispatchs and share URLs, polluting the feed with irreversible duplicates.
  Recommendation: Split preview/render from persistent creation, or require an idempotency key derived from scope+window+voice+generate inputs with server-side dedupe. Also specify whether users can delete/archive duplicate dispatches.
- [medium] `404` is overloaded as "unpushed" in the CLI flow, which will mask authorization failures as local-state issues (specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md:160-167)
  The local-mode fallback treats a `404` from the batch-analysis API as proof that a checkpoint is merely unpushed and tells the user to `git push`. But the companion web spec already uses `404` to hide unauthorized resources instead of leaking existence. If the batch/org APIs follow the same access-control pattern, pushed checkpoints from repos the caller no longer has access to will be silently dropped and misreported as "unpushed," making real permission failures hard to detect and recover from. This finding depends on the reasonable inference that the new APIs will follow the same anti-enumeration convention.
  Recommendation: Define a distinct per-checkpoint status for `forbidden`/`not_visible` separate from `unknown`/`unpushed`, and require the CLI to surface permission failures separately instead of folding them into the push hint.

Next steps:
- Specify mandatory repo-level authorization rules for all new dispatch/org endpoints.
- Add idempotent create semantics or a non-persistent preview/read path before shipping.
- Separate unauthorized vs unpushed checkpoint states in the batch-analysis contract.

input.new_string:
### Unpushed-checkpoint detection

**Purely local signal — no API needed.** Before any batch fetch, enumerate the set of checkpoint-commits that exist on the local `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch but are missing from the remote tracking branch:

```
git rev-list entire/checkpoints/v1 ^origin/entire/checkpoints/v1
```

Each returned commit carries a checkpoint ID in its trailer (see CLAUDE.md). That's the unpushed set — deterministically known from git refs, not inferred from API responses. Both modes use the same local method:

- **Local mode**: after computing the unpushed set, the CLI can optionally skip the batch analysis fetch for those IDs (they'll return `unknown` anyway) or include them and expect `unknown`.
- **Server mode**: the server only sees pushed checkpoints. The CLI enumerates local checkpoints in the window and intersects with the unpushed set; the delta is what should have been on the server but wasn't reported — that's the unpushed nudge.

**Edge case: no remote tracking branch.** If `origin/entire/checkpoints/v1` doesn't exist (user has never pushed the checkpoint branch), all local checkpoints in the window are "unpushed." The nudge wording changes to: `"⚠ you haven't pushed your checkpoint branch — run \`git push origin entire/checkpoints/v1\` to enable richer analysis."`

**Distinctions surfaced to the user** (each counted and labelled separately — not conflated):

| Classification | Source | User-visible label |
|---|---|---|
| `unpushed` | local git refs | "N checkpoints not pushed — run `git push …`" |
| `access_denied` | API status `not_visible` | "N checkpoints you no longer have access to" |
| `pipeline_pending` | API status `pending`/`generating` | "N checkpoints still being analyzed" |
| `pipeline_failed` | API status `failed` | "N checkpoints failed analysis" |
| `uncategorized` | all fallback steps exhausted | "N uncategorized checkpoints skipped" |

In `--format text`/`markdown`, these are grouped into one warnings block at the bottom. In `--format json`, they live under `warnings.{unpushed_count, access_denied_count, pending_count, failed_count, uncategorized_count}`.

+   - `unknown` → the server has never seen this checkpoint ID. Fall through to step 2. Unpushed status is determined locally (next section), not inferred from this response.

2. **Local summarize title** — if summarization is enabled (`settings.IsSummarizeEnabled()`) and a `Summary.Title` exists for the checkpoint in `entire/checkpoints/v1/<id>/…/metadata.json`, use it. No labels → checkpoint lands in a flat "Updates" section for its repo.
3. **Commit message subject** — if the checkpoint has an associated commit via the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, use the subject line. No labels → "Updates".
4. **None of the above** — omit the checkpoint from output. Count reported at end: `"N uncategorized checkpoints skipped."`

### Unpushed-checkpoint detection

**Purely local signal — no API needed.** Before any batch fetch, enumerate the set of checkpoint-commits that exist on the local `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch but are missing from the remote tracking branch:

```
git rev-list entire/checkpoints/v1 ^origin/entire/checkpoints/v1
```

Each returned commit carries a checkpoint ID in its trailer (see CLAUDE.md). That's the unpushed set — deterministically known from git refs, not inferred from API responses. Both modes use the same local method:

- **Local mode**: after computing the unpushed set, the CLI can skip the batch analysis fetch for those IDs (or include them and expect `unknown` from the response — the local set is the source of truth either way).
- **Server mode**: the server only sees pushed checkpoints. CLI enumerates local checkpoints in the window and marks the unpushed set (by git), independent of anything in the server response.

**Edge case: no remote tracking branch.** If `origin/entire/checkpoints/v1` doesn't exist (user has never pushed the checkpoint branch), all local checkpoints in the window are "unpushed." The nudge wording becomes: `"⚠ you haven't pushed your checkpoint branch — run \`git push origin entire/checkpoints/v1\` to enable richer analysis."`

**Per-classification warnings surfaced separately** (no conflation of unrelated conditions):

| Classification | Source of truth | Text-mode line |
|---|---|---|
| `unpushed_count` | local git refs | `⚠ N checkpoints not pushed — run \`git push origin entire/checkpoints/v1\`` |
| `access_denied_count` | API status `not_visible` | `⚠ N checkpoints you no longer have access to` |
| `pending_count` | API status `pending`/`generating` | `⏳ N checkpoints still being analyzed (retry in a minute or use --wait)` |
| `failed_count` | API status `failed` | `✕ N checkpoints failed analysis on the server` |
| `uncategorized_count` | all fallback steps exhausted | `N uncategorized checkpoints skipped` |

In `--format text`/`markdown` these render as separate lines in the warnings block; in `--format json` they live under `warnings.<name>`.

### Server-side prerequisites

- `POST /api/v1/users/me/checkpoints/analyses/batch` — **exists** (see analysis-endpoints PR). Used in `--local` mode. **Authorization required**: server MUST enforce per-checkpoint access (each ID's repo must be visible to the caller). IDs the caller cannot see return status `not_visible`, not `unknown`, so the CLI can distinguish access-denied from truly-unknown.
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` — **new, required for default mode**. Takes scope params + generate/voice, returns the structured dispatch payload + `web_url`. Persists result so entire.io web can render. See authorization and idempotency sections below.
- `GET /api/v1/orgs/:org/checkpoints?since=…&cursor=…` — **new, required for `--org --local`** only. Server-mode `--org` uses internal enumeration, so this endpoint isn't blocking for the default path. **Authorization required**: response filters to repos the caller has access to within the requested org; mixed-access orgs return only the visible subset (and never leak repo names/IDs outside that subset).

#### Authorization contract (required for all new endpoints)

**All dispatch-related endpoints MUST enforce per-repo authorization before any work or persistence.** Authentication (a valid login token) is necessary but not sufficient.

Specifically:

- `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` — when the body names `repo`, the caller must have access to that repo; reject with 403 if not. When the body names `org`, resolve to the set of repos in that org the caller has access to (intersection with org membership) — if empty, return 404 rather than a zero-result dispatch (don't persist empty dispatches).
- `GET /api/v1/dispatches/:id` — caller must have access to **every** repo the dispatch covers (strict mode, matches the web UI spec). On failure, return 404 (don't leak existence).
- `GET /api/v1/orgs/:org/checkpoints` — filter results to repos the caller has access to in that org. If the caller has zero access in that org, 404.
- Batch analyses — per-ID access check; inaccessible IDs return `not_visible`, not the content.

Access snapshots at creation time are recorded on the dispatch record so later revocations don't retroactively hide a dispatch from the user who created it (history preservation — see web UI spec).

#### Idempotency

**`POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` MUST be idempotent** on a deterministic key derived from the request inputs. Rationale: any retry (CLI retry on 5xx, user re-running the same command, accidental double-submit from the web UI) would otherwise pollute the feed with duplicate dispatches.

**Idempotency key** = stable hash (e.g., SHA-256) of:

```
user_id
+ scope (ordered: [repo] OR sorted([org/repo, …]) for org scope)
+ since (ISO, truncated to minute)
+ until (ISO, truncated to minute)
+ sorted(branches) (or "all")
+ generate (bool)
+ voice (normalized: preset name → preset name; file content → hash of content; literal → hash of literal string)
```

Server behavior:

- Compute the key on request receipt.
- If an existing dispatch with the same key exists and is `status: complete` or `status: generating`, return that dispatch's id/web_url — do not create a duplicate.
- `regenerate` (`POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches/:id/regenerate`) explicitly bypasses dedupe — it's the documented escape hatch for "I want a new run of the same scope."
- Dry-run requests (`dry_run: true`) are never persisted and never dedupe-checked.

**Client-side retry semantics**: CLI can safely retry 5xx without worrying about duplicates, because the server keys on content not request id. No client-provided `Idempotency-Key` header required, but the server MAY accept one if supplied to cover cases where scope inputs are identical but the user really wants a separate record.

**Deletion / cleanup** — users can delete their own dispatches via `DELETE /api/v1/dispatches/:id` (creator only; also enforces access). Deletion is hard-delete in v1; soft-delete + restore deferred. This prevents feed pollution if duplicates slip through somehow, and gives users agency over their history.

#### Response shape for `POST /dispatches`

```json
{
  "id": "dsp_01H…",
  "idempotency_key_hash": "sha256:…",   /* echoed so callers can verify */
  "deduped": false,                      /* true if server returned existing record without creating a new one */
  "web_url": "https://entire.io/dispatch/dsp_01H…",
  "window": {"since": "…", "until": "…"},
  "repos": [ /* same shape as --format json output below */ ],
  "totals": { "checkpoints": 13, "branches": 4, "files_touched": 23 },
  "warnings": {
    "unpushed_count": 2,
    "access_denied_count": 0,
    "pending_count": 0,
    "failed_count": 0,
    "uncategorized_count": 0
  },
  "generated_text": "…"  /* only when `generate: true` in request; null otherwise */
}
```

+ voice (normalized: preset name → preset name; file content → hash of content; literal → hash of literal string)

- If an existing dispatch with the same key exists and is `status: complete` or `status: generating`, return that dispatch's id/web_url — do not create a duplicate.

- Dry-run requests (`dry_run: true`) are never persisted and never dedupe-checked.

## Access control

**Strict** — a user can view a dispatch only if they have access to **every** repo the dispatch covers. For an `--org`-scoped dispatch, access is required to every repo the dispatch actually includes (which is the intersection of the org's repos and the creator's access at creation time, not the org's entire repo list).

**Authorization is mandatory on every dispatch endpoint** — authentication alone is never enough. Details:

- `GET /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` (list) — returns only dispatches the viewer passes the strict check for. Must not leak titles or counts for dispatches covering repos the viewer lacks access to.
- `GET /api/v1/dispatches/:id` (detail) — 404 on access failure (not 403 — don't leak existence).
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` (create) — creator must have access to every repo in the resolved scope at creation time:
  - For `repo: "owner/name"`, verify access to that specific repo.
  - For `org: "name"`, resolve to the intersection of the org's repos and the creator's access list. Use that filtered set as the dispatch's scope. If the intersection is empty, return 404 (do not persist an empty dispatch).
  - The resolved access boundary is snapshotted onto the dispatch record; later revocations do not retroactively hide a dispatch from the user who created it (history preservation).
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches/:id/regenerate` — both: (a) the caller must own the original dispatch OR have access to every repo it covers, and (b) the caller must still have access to every repo at regeneration time (this is a fresh creation, so stale access doesn't carry over).
- `DELETE /api/v1/dispatches/:id` — creator-only. Non-creators get 403 even if they can view it.

**Required server-side tests** for mixed-access scenarios: user has access to repo A but not repo B; attempts to create an org dispatch covering both; server must reject or filter to A only, never silently include B.

# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: working tree diff
Verdict: needs-attention

No-ship: the spec still has a real auth hole on regenerate, the new idempotency rule can freeze stale results instead of making retries safe, and the 404/unpushed split now relies on git state that is not authoritative.

Findings:
- [high] `regenerate` lets any viewer replay another user's dispatch configuration (specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-web-ui-design.md:45)
  The access rule for `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches/:id/regenerate` allows callers who are not the creator to regenerate as long as they can view every repo in the dispatch. That is not just a read check: the endpoint is defined to create a new dispatch with the same scope and voice as the original. In this spec, voices can be custom text or uploaded markdown, so this implies the server will reuse stored user-supplied prompt material for a non-owner. The likely impact is that any authorized viewer can spend compute on someone else’s dispatch configuration and potentially replay private custom voice content. Make regenerate creator-only, or require non-owners to submit a fresh voice payload and never reuse stored custom voice data across users.
  Recommendation: Tighten `regenerate` to creator-only, or split it into a creator-only clone endpoint plus a separate create flow where other viewers must provide their own voice inputs.
- [high] Create-idempotency dedupes against request shape, not source state, so retries can return permanently stale dispatches (specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md:402-423)
  The proposed idempotency key is derived only from the request inputs, and the server returns an existing dispatch even when that dispatch is already `complete`. That means the first result for a given scope/window can become sticky even after the underlying checkpoint state changes: a checkpoint that was previously `pending`, `failed`, or locally unpushed can later become analyzable, but the same create request still resolves to the old record instead of producing a fresh dispatch. This breaks the claim that callers can safely retry without side effects; in real use it turns retries into stale-cache hits and forces users onto the special-case regenerate path to get up-to-date output. Limit dedupe to in-flight / short retry windows, or include a source-state version in the key (for example the checkpoint set plus analysis freshness/version metadata).
  Recommendation: Change idempotency to collapse duplicate submissions only while a request is in flight or within a short TTL, or key it on request inputs plus a server-side source revision so reruns after data changes produce a new dispatch.
- [medium] The new unpushed detection treats local remote-ref state as authoritative when it is not (specs/2026-04-16-entire-dispatch-design.md:179-190)
  The spec now declares `git rev-list entire/checkpoints/v1 ^origin/entire/checkpoints/v1` the source of truth for unpushed checkpoints and even suggests skipping batch analysis fetches for those IDs. That is not actually deterministic: remote-tracking refs are stale until fetched, and this hardcodes `origin` instead of the branch’s configured upstream. A checkpoint already present on the server can therefore be mislabeled as unpushed, which suppresses cloud analysis, inflates `unpushed_count`, and reintroduces exactly the 404/unpushed ambiguity this change is trying to remove. Use the real upstream ref and refresh/validate it before treating a checkpoint as unpushed, or keep this as an advisory hint instead of the authoritative classifier.
  Recommendation: Resolve the actual upstream for `entire/checkpoints/v1`, refresh the remote-tracking ref before comparison, and do not skip server analysis solely because local git metadata says a checkpoint is unpushed.

Next steps:
- Make `regenerate` creator-only or require a fresh caller-supplied voice payload.
- Redefine create idempotency so it only dedupes retries, not later reruns against changed checkpoint/analysis state.
- Replace the hardcoded local `origin/...` check with upstream-aware, refreshed remote state before classifying checkpoints as unpushed.

- `GET /api/v1/orgs/:org/checkpoints` — filter results to repos the caller has access to in that org. If the caller has zero access in that org, 404.
- Batch analyses — per-ID access check; inaccessible IDs return `not_visible`, not the content.

Access snapshots at creation time are recorded on the dispatch record so later revocations don't retroactively hide a dispatch from the user who created it (history preservation — see web UI spec).

#### Idempotency

**`POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` MUST be idempotent** on a deterministic key derived from the request inputs. Rationale: any retry (CLI retry on 5xx, user re-running the same command, accidental double-submit from the web UI) would otherwise pollute the feed with duplicate dispatches.

**Idempotency key** = stable hash (e.g., SHA-256) of:

```
user_id
+ scope (ordered: [repo] OR sorted([org/repo, …]) for org scope)
+ since (ISO, truncated to minute)
+ until (ISO, truncated to minute)
+ sorted(branches) (or "all")
+ generate (bool)
+ voice (normalized: preset name → preset name; file content → hash of content; literal → hash of literal string)
```

Server behavior:

- Compute the key on request receipt.
- If an existing dispatch with the same key exists and is `status: complete` or `status: generating`, return that dispatch's id/web_url — do not create a duplicate.
- `regenerate` (`POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches/:id/regenerate`) explicitly bypasses dedupe — it's the documented escape hatch for "I want a new run of the same scope."
- Dry-run requests (`dry_run: true`) are never persisted and never dedupe-checked.

**Client-side retry semantics**: CLI can safely retry 5xx without worrying about duplicates, because the server keys on content not request id. No client-provided `Idempotency-Key` header required, but the server MAY accept one if supplied to cover cases where scope inputs are identical but the user really wants a separate record.

# Spec simplification — responding to follow-up adversarial review

## Context

The follow-up Codex adversarial review on the `entire dispatch` specs raised three issues:

1. **Regenerate auth hole** — any viewer with access to every repo can regenerate someone else's dispatch, potentially replaying private voice content.
2. **Idempotency cache-staleness** — fingerprint keyed only on request inputs (including relative `since`/`until`) freezes output even after checkpoint state changes, so retries return stale results and force users into the `regenerate` special case.
3. **Unpushed detection unreliable** — `git rev-list entire/checkpoints/v1 ^origin/entire/checkpoints/v1` depends on stale remote-tracking refs and hardcodes `origin`, so it re-introduces the same 404/unpushed ambiguity it was meant to resolve.

The user's response to all three is to simplify rather than fortify:

1. **Remove `regenerate` entirely.** With a better fingerprint (see #2), re-submitting the same inputs to `POST /dispatches` naturally returns the same dispatch when source state is unchanged and produces a fresh one when it isn't. Regenerate becomes redundant and its auth hole disappears with it.
2. **Rebuild the fingerprint on actual source state** — use the real first and last checkpoint timestamps (of the checkpoints that actually contributed bullets) plus the count of used checkpoints. Same set + same inputs → dedupe; any checkpoint added/removed/newly-complete → new fingerprint → new dispatch.
3. **Drop unpushed detection from v1.** No local-git heuristics. The server's batch-analysis status model already distinguishes `complete`/`pending`/`generating`/`failed`/`not_visible`/`unknown`, and "unknown" just falls through the local fallback chain without trying to diagnose why. Users who want to confirm push state use their own git tools.

content.text:
Good challenge — let me think through this carefully.

**Why timestamps are awkward here:**
- Multi-repo: merging checkpoints from repos A and B produces one combined first/last timestamp, losing per-repo resolution. Two unrelated sets with matching boundary dates + count would collide (rare, but the fingerprint should be airtight).
- Timestamps are stable per checkpoint, but the fingerprint uses only 2 of them — the interior of the set is invisible to the hash.

**Why "first/last checkpoint IDs" is also awkward:**
- Checkpoint IDs are random 12-hex strings — they don't have inherent temporal order. "First" and "last" only mean something if you sort them by timestamp, which pushes you back to timestamps anyway. Sorting lexically is arbitrary.

**The cleanest fix: hash the entire sorted set of used checkpoint IDs.**
- Multi-repo: trivial — union all used IDs across all repos, sort lex, hash. One scalar, no special case.
- Perfect uniqueness: any single checkpoint added/removed/newly-eligible → different hash → new dispatch.
- `used_count` becomes redundant in the hash but is worth keeping in the *response* for human-readable debugging.
- Per-repo first/last timestamps still show up in the response payload (for UI metadata), just not in the fingerprint.

  2. Batch-fetch analyses (cheap — cached per-checkpoint).

  4. Compute `used_checkpoints_hash = sha256(lex_sorted(used_ids).join(","))`.
  5. Compute fingerprint from the components above.
  6. If a completed dispatch exists with the same fingerprint: return it with `deduped: true`. Skip LLM synthesis.
  7. Otherwise: run LLM synthesis (if `generate: true`), persist a new dispatch, return with `deduped: false`.

A pending checkpoint becoming complete also changes the used set (it joins the list), so the dispatch refreshes automatically. Multi-repo is handled naturally because we hash one flat sorted list, not a per-repo structure. Solves Codex's stale-cache concern without a regenerate endpoint.

# Spec simplification — responding to follow-up adversarial review

## Context

The follow-up Codex adversarial review on the `entire dispatch` specs raised three issues:

1. **Regenerate auth hole** — any viewer with access to every repo can regenerate someone else's dispatch, potentially replaying private voice content.
2. **Idempotency cache-staleness** — fingerprint keyed only on request inputs (including relative `since`/`until`) freezes output even after checkpoint state changes, so retries return stale results and force users into the `regenerate` special case.
3. **Unpushed detection unreliable** — `git rev-list entire/checkpoints/v1 ^origin/entire/checkpoints/v1` depends on stale remote-tracking refs and hardcodes `origin`, so it re-introduces the same 404/unpushed ambiguity it was meant to resolve.

Honest look at what regenerate was doing in our spec:

**Originally introduced for:**
- Pipeline lagging — dispatch created when some checkpoints were still `pending`. User wants to refresh after analyses complete.
- Underlying data changes — new checkpoints added, access revoked, etc.
- Voice template edited with same filename.
- LLM reshuffle — same inputs, just want different wording.

**What the new source-state fingerprint covers automatically (no regenerate needed):**
- Pipeline lag → when more checkpoints complete and join the "used" set, `used_checkpoints_hash` changes → re-submitting `POST /dispatches` produces a new dispatch. ✓
- Data changes (adds, removes, access revocations) → same mechanism. ✓
- Voice file edited → `voice` is normalized to a content hash, so edits change the fingerprint. ✓

**What regenerate uniquely does that nothing else does:**
- LLM reshuffle — exact same inputs + exact same source state, just roll the dice on the LLM again.

That's the only remaining use case. And honestly, it's edge:
- Most users calling "regenerate" are actually trying to refresh after state changed (cases 1–3), not reshuffle prose.
- If someone really wants different wording, they can nudge the voice ("add a sentence about …") — that changes the voice hash → new fingerprint → new dispatch.
- They can also `DELETE` + re-submit to force a new record.

**My read: regenerate was a speculative nice-to-have**, not structurally required. Removing it shrinks the spec, closes the Codex auth hole, and costs us only the LLM-reshuffle case which has workarounds.

**Purely local signal — no API needed.** Before any batch fetch, enumerate the set of checkpoint-commits that exist on the local `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch but are missing from the remote tracking branch:

```

```

Each returned commit carries a checkpoint ID in its trailer (see CLAUDE.md). That's the unpushed set — deterministically known from git refs, not inferred from API responses. Both modes use the same local method:

- **Local mode**: after computing the unpushed set, the CLI can skip the batch analysis fetch for those IDs (or include them and expect `unknown` from the response — the local set is the source of truth either way).

**Edge case: no remote tracking branch.** If `origin/entire/checkpoints/v1` doesn't exist (user has never pushed the checkpoint branch), all local checkpoints in the window are "unpushed." input.new_string:
#### Idempotency

**`POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` MUST be idempotent** on a deterministic key derived from both the request inputs AND the actual source state (the set of checkpoints that will produce bullets). Rationale: request-input-only keys make retries safe but turn legitimate refreshes (pending → complete, new checkpoints, revocations) into permanent stale-cache hits. Including source state means same inputs + same data = dedupe; same inputs + changed data = fresh dispatch.

**Idempotency key** = stable SHA-256 hash of:

```
user_id
+ scope (ordered: [repo] OR sorted([org/repo, …]) for org scope)
+ used_checkpoints_hash  // sha256(lex_sorted(used_checkpoint_ids).join(","))
+ sorted(branches) (or "all")
+ generate (bool)
+ voice (normalized: preset name → preset name; file content → hash of content; literal → hash of literal string)
```

`used_checkpoints_hash` is the SHA-256 of the lex-sorted list of checkpoint IDs that actually contributed a bullet (i.e., passed the fallback chain). Multi-repo case is trivial: the list is the union of used IDs across all covered repos, sorted lex — one scalar in the fingerprint regardless of repo count.

**Response-only metadata** (present in the response but NOT in the fingerprint):

- `first_checkpoint_created_at`, `last_checkpoint_created_at` — human-readable window boundaries for UI labels and CLI text output. Derived from the used set.
- `used_checkpoint_count` — redundant with `used_checkpoints_hash` for uniqueness, but useful for at-a-glance metadata and debugging.
- `used_checkpoints_hash` — echoed in the response so clients can verify/debug.

**Order of operations on the server**:

1. Resolve access + enumerate candidate checkpoints in the request's window (cheap — metadata only).
2. Batch-fetch analyses (cheap — cached per-checkpoint).
3. Apply the fallback chain to determine the "used" set (checkpoints that will contribute a bullet).
4. Compute `used_checkpoints_hash = sha256(lex_sorted(used_ids).join(","))`.
5. Compute fingerprint from the components above.
6. If a completed dispatch exists with the same fingerprint: return it with `deduped: true`. Skip LLM synthesis.
7. Otherwise: run LLM synthesis (if `generate: true`), persist a new dispatch, return with `deduped: false`.

**Why hashing the used set is sufficient**: any single checkpoint added, removed, or newly eligible changes the sorted ID list → changes `used_checkpoints_hash` → changes the fingerprint → produces a fresh dispatch. A previously-pending checkpoint becoming complete also changes the used set (it joins the list), so the dispatch refreshes automatically on next submission. Multi-repo is handled naturally because we hash one flat sorted list, not a per-repo structure.

**No `regenerate` endpoint**: with the source-state fingerprint, re-submitting `POST /dispatches` with the same inputs is the natural refresh mechanism. If source state hasn't changed, the same record is returned (`deduped: true`). If it has, a fresh record is produced. There is no separate bypass-dedupe endpoint.

#### Idempotency

**`POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` MUST be idempotent** on a deterministic key derived from both the request inputs AND the actual source state (the set of checkpoints that will produce bullets). Rationale: request-input-only keys make retries safe but turn legitimate refreshes (pending → complete, new checkpoints, revocations) into permanent stale-cache hits. Including source state means same inputs + same data = dedupe; same inputs + changed data = fresh dispatch.

**Idempotency key** = stable SHA-256 hash of:

```
user_id
+ scope (ordered: [repo] OR sorted([org/repo, …]) for org scope)
+ used_checkpoints_hash  // sha256(lex_sorted(used_checkpoint_ids).join(","))
+ sorted(branches) (or "all")
+ generate (bool)
+ voice (normalized: preset name → preset name; file content → hash of content; literal → hash of literal string)
```

`used_checkpoints_hash` is the SHA-256 of the lex-sorted list of checkpoint IDs that actually contributed a bullet (i.e., passed the fallback chain). Multi-repo case is trivial: the list is the union of used IDs across all covered repos, sorted lex — one scalar in the fingerprint regardless of repo count.

**Response-only metadata** (present in the response but NOT in the fingerprint):

- `first_checkpoint_created_at`, `last_checkpoint_created_at` — human-readable window boundaries for UI labels and CLI text output. Derived from the used set.
- `used_checkpoint_count` — redundant with `used_checkpoints_hash` for uniqueness, but useful for at-a-glance metadata and debugging.
- `used_checkpoints_hash` — echoed in the response so clients can verify/debug.

**Order of operations on the server**:

1. Resolve access + enumerate candidate checkpoints in the request's window (cheap — metadata only).
2. Batch-fetch analyses (cheap — cached per-checkpoint).
3. Apply the fallback chain to determine the "used" set (checkpoints that will contribute a bullet).
4. Compute `used_checkpoints_hash = sha256(lex_sorted(used_ids).join(","))`.
5. Compute fingerprint from the components above.
6. If a completed dispatch exists with the same fingerprint: return it with `deduped: true`. Skip LLM synthesis.
7. Otherwise: run LLM synthesis (if `generate: true`), persist a new dispatch, return with `deduped: false`.

A previously-pending checkpoint becoming complete also changes the used set (it joins the list), so the dispatch refreshes automatically on next submission. Multi-repo is handled naturally because we hash one flat sorted list, not a per-repo structure.

## Open questions / future work

1. **`--org` endpoint shape** — needs to be designed alongside the API team. Specifically: does it return checkpoint IDs only, or also enough metadata (repo, commit SHA) to skip the per-repo batch fetch? If the former, we do one enumeration call + one batch per repo. If the latter, one call does everything.
2. **Rate limits for large orgs** — an org with 500 checkpoints/week will do 3 batch calls (200 max each). Fine. An org with 10,000 checkpoints/week (large teams) starts hitting rate limits. Probably not an immediate concern; revisit if users report.
3. **Voice preset library** — v1 ships `neutral` and `marvin`. Future candidates: `plain`, `changelog`, `standup`, `release-notes`. Presets are plain markdown files in `cmd/entire/cli/dispatch/voices/`, embedded at build time; adding one is a code-free-ish drop-in. User-defined saved voices (e.g., `~/.config/entire/voices/`) deferred to post-v1.
4. **"Since last dispatch" mode** — currently user has to remember `--since` value. A `--since last-dispatch` mode that reads a timestamp from `.entire/state/last-dispatch` could be nice. Deferred to post-v1.
5. **Additional output formats** — current spec covers `text` (default) and `markdown`. Future candidates: `html` (email-ready), `rss` (for feed-driven newsletters), `slack` (Slack-flavored markdown). Deferred to post-v1.

## Interactive wizard

`entire dispatch` with no flags on a TTY auto-enters a `huh`-based wizard. Matches the codebase convention (`entire sessions stop`, `entire search`). With any flag passed, or stdin piped, the wizard is skipped and the command runs non-interactively.

### Trigger rules

- **Wizard ON** — stdin is a TTY AND no flags have been explicitly set.
- **Wizard OFF** — any flag passed (including flags with default-equal values), stdin is piped, or `ACCESSIBLE=1` with no flags (accessible mode uses `NewAccessibleForm()` internally, so wizard still shows but in accessible form).

### Step sequence

1. **Source mode** — Server (default, Entire's tokens) / Local (user's tokens). Maps to `--local`.
2. **Scope** — Current repo / Specific repos (disabled in server mode) / Whole org (prompts for org name) / Custom (jump to freeform flag review).
3. **Time window** — Last 24h / Last 7d (default) / Last 30d / Custom (text input accepting git-style or ISO).
4. **Branches** — Current branch / All branches / Select specific (multi-select from local refs).
5. **Generate prose?** — Bullets only / Generate full dispatch with voice (default in wizard). Maps to `--generate`. If "bullets only", skip step 6.
6. **Voice** (only shown if step 5 = generate) — Neutral product update (default) / Marvin (sardonic AI, Entire Dispatch style) / Custom (text input) / Load from markdown file (file picker).
7. **Format** — Text (default) / Markdown / JSON.
8. **Confirm & run** — Shows the equivalent CLI command, then asks: Run it now (default) / Copy command to clipboard and exit / Edit flags (jumps back to step 1) / Cancel.

Every step has a default that works on Enter; power users can tab through in a few seconds.

## Access control

**Strict** — a user can view a dispatch only if they have access to **every** repo the dispatch covers. For an `--org`-scoped dispatch, access is required to every repo the dispatch actually includes (which is the intersection of the org's repos and the creator's access at creation time, not the org's entire repo list).

**Authorization is mandatory on every dispatch endpoint** — authentication alone is never enough. Details:

- `GET /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` (list) — returns only dispatches the viewer passes the strict check for. Must not leak titles or counts for dispatches covering repos the viewer lacks access to.
- `GET /api/v1/dispatches/:id` (detail) — 404 on access failure (not 403 — don't leak existence).
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches` (create) — creator must have access to every repo in the resolved scope at creation time:
  - For `repo: "owner/name"`, verify access to that specific repo.
  - For `org: "name"`, resolve to the intersection of the org's repos and the creator's access list. Use that filtered set as the dispatch's scope. If the intersection is empty, return 404 (do not persist an empty dispatch).
  - The resolved access boundary is snapshotted onto the dispatch record; later revocations do not retroactively hide a dispatch from the user who created it (history preservation).
- `POST /api/v1/users/me/dispatches/:id/regenerate` — both: (a) the caller must own the original dispatch OR have access to every repo it covers, and (b) the caller must still have access to every repo at regeneration time (this is a fresh creation, so stale access doesn't carry over).
- `DELETE /api/v1/dispatches/:id` — creator-only. Non-creators get 403 even if they can view it.

**Required server-side tests** for mixed-access scenarios: user has access to repo A but not repo B; attempts to create an org dispatch covering both; server must reject or filter to A only, never silently include B.

## Routes

| Route | Purpose | Auth |
|---|---|---|
| `/dispatches` | Personal feed — all dispatches viewer has access to | `_authenticated` |
| `/dispatches/new` | Create form | `_authenticated` |
| `/dispatches/:id` | Detail page | `_authenticated` + strict access check |
| `/gh/:org/:repo/dispatches` | Per-repo filtered index | `_authenticated` + repo access check |

Follows the existing TanStack Router conventions in the codebase (`_authenticated/*.tsx`, `_repo/gh/$org.$repo.*.tsx`).

## Pages

### Detail page — `/dispatches/:id`

**Layout**: two-column. Main column renders the dispatch markdown (same payload as `--format markdown` from the CLI). Right sidebar (280px) shows metadata.

**Main column** — rendered markdown:

- Title: `Weekly dispatch — entireio/cli` (or similar; generated or user-provided)
- Meta line under title: date range · branches · checkpoint count · file count
- Body: themed sections with bullets (same as CLI output)
- When generated with a voice preset, voice intro/outro render with a subtle visual treatment (e.g., italic + colored bar) so voice-authored lines are distinguishable from bullet content.

**Sidebar** sections, top to bottom:

- **Creator** — avatar, name, `@handle`, "2h ago" relative time.
- **Scope** — repo badges, window, branches, voice name.
- **Actions** (buttons):
  - `Regenerate` (primary) — reruns the same scope + voice; new dispatch, keeps original. Loading state inline.
  - `Copy markdown` — clipboard copy of the raw markdown payload.
  - `Open in CLI` — opens a modal showing the equivalent `entire dispatch …` command with a Copy button.
  - `Copy share link` — copies the current URL.

**Empty / error states**:

- Dispatch not found or no access → 404 page (same layout as rest of site).
- Dispatch still generating → loading skeleton, poll status every 2s, render when complete.
- Generation failed → error card with reason + "Retry" button.

### Personal feed — `/dispatches`

**Layout**: one-column list.

**Header** — "Dispatches" + filter bar:

- Repo filter (multi-select, default "All repos")
- Date range (preset: Last 7d / Last 30d / All time, or custom)
